verdict.rationale: RevenueCat ships Rico, a built-in assistant that answers plain-language questions about subscription data, and it offers AI-prompted paywall generation and editing. Both are first-party AI features inside the product, but the evidence shows only Q&A analysis and paywall drafting, not broader task delegation where the assistant acts on the user's behalf. The MCP server and AI Toolkit serve external agents, so they are not credited as a built-in assistant. Missing for 10: evidence that Rico can execute actions (e.g., configuring products, entitlements or offerings) in the dashboard, documentation of its scope and limits, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Instead of digging through charts and tables yourself, you can ask Rico plain-language questions like "Why did MRR drop in Germany last week?" and get a direct, data-driven answer.
Launch faster with fully customizable Paywalls that start from a template, AI-prompt or  a blank canvass.
